question: Whether WinINet's capture keeps a request body its client writes in pieces - the head sent with HttpSendRequestEx, the body with InternetWriteFile, the request ended with HttpEndRequest - as it keeps one handed to HttpSendRequest whole, and in which buffers.
answer: As a whole body is kept, a buffer to a write: each piece the client wrote is one buffer, in order, numbered from 0 and flagged at its ends - a piece past 64,511 bytes cut there, as a whole body is cut - and the body ends with an empty buffer flagged last. Every part matched the server's truth, synchronously and asynchronously, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, and eight clients at once; nothing was lost.

probe.tool: tools/InterCat.WinInetProbe --write n [--bytes 262144] [--async] [--http2] [--concurrency 8], 16 exchanges each or 64 eight at once, beside a decoy outside the process filter; the client logs each piece it wrote by length and SHA-256, in order

runs.run: pieces of up to 80,000 bytes, bodies to 256 KiB
pieces of up to 80,000 bytes over HTTP/2
pieces of up to 4,096 bytes, eight at once, its buffers' metadata kept

capture.command: icat record --profile content --source etw/manifest/Microsoft-Windows-WinINet-Capture --mechanism http --pid <workload> --channel * --max-record-bytes 65536 --max-session-bytes 67108864 --inspection hex-text --duration 25, beside InterCat.TestWorkloads http-wininet --requests 64 --start-after 8 --write n [--bytes 262144] [--concurrency 8]; then icat exchanges --exchanges 10000 --decode, and each part of each exchange saved by icat content --part and matched by SHA-256

runs.run: pieces of up to 80,000 bytes, bodies to 256 KiB
pieces of up to 4,096 bytes, eight at once

ledger: fixtures/FX-HTTP-007/evidence/eight-at-once/buffers.csv: each buffer the probe captured of its 64 exchanges, in time order - its 100 ns readings after the first, event, exchange number, place, ends, length, the request its exchange's head named, and whether a thread that made a request raised it - never its bytes. A test groups it as a session's records are grouped, and holds each body to its client's writes.
note: A body's buffers are matched with the pieces its client wrote by their lengths in order, the empty buffer that ends it aside; a piece past 64,511 bytes, which no ETW event holds whole, is cut into buffers of 64,511 and the rest. Request 0's body is empty: the client writes nothing, and no record is raised for it. Neither the truth nor this file holds a byte of what was sent or read.
